sites.notes: Hard-capped at 90 reviews per product, always — fetchNordstromBVViaScripting (background-v2.js) loops a fixed 9 pages x 10 (args: [apiKey, numericId, 10, 9]) and only stops early if a page comes back empty or the running total already reaches the product's own totalResults. So a product with <=90 reviews gets 100% coverage; anything above 90 gets exactly 90/total. Live-measured (2026-08-01) against three real 200+-review Nordstrom products using the NORDSTROM_BV_DEBUG_COVERAGE logging added for this purpose: 33%, 48%, and 26% coverage (avg ~36%) — all well under "large majority," confirming "limited" over "true." Consistent with the same 90-review-cap mechanism measured on macys.com/bloomingdales.com/urbanoutfitters.com/freepeople.com — coverage on any given product is a function of that product's total review count (min(90, totalReviews) / totalReviews), not a fixed retailer-wide rate, so these three numbers are illustrative data points rather than a guarantee for every product. Debug logging remains in place for future re-verification — look for '[bustfit][COVERAGE]' lines in the service worker console.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 after a real beta-tester bug report (gray dot — extension not recognizing the page at all). This entry previously listed the domain as 'rack.nordstrom.com', which is NOT a real, resolvable hostname (DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN, confirmed live) — the real domain is nordstromrack.com, a genuinely separate top-level domain, not a subdomain of nordstrom.com. That wrong domain string was used consistently across manifest.json (content_scripts.matches/host_permissions — meaning content.js was never even injected on the real site), content.js (_APPROVED_DOMAINS, getRetailer(), the RETAILERS key, BV_DOMAINS, the isNordstrom microdata gate), and background-v2.js (_supportedAutoOpenUrl()) — this file and content.js's RETAILERS table had agreed with each other the whole time, which is why validate-supported-sites.js's pre-existing checks never caught it (see that file's new Check B2 for the fix: it now confirms every domain is actually covered by manifest.json, not just cross-checked between these two files). The 'shares Nordstrom's platform' assumption behind this entry was never live-validated before now — every earlier attempt hit sandbox bot-detection, and this was correctly flagged as 'inconclusive' during an earlier badge-collision sweep, but that flag was never wired to block the supported-sites status. Full incident writeup in RETAILER_SCRAPERS.md. Now live-validated directly (real Chrome, no bot-detection encountered on any page checked): genuinely shared with Nordstrom — JSON-LD Product shape, the reviewBody-text-lives-in-the-content-attribute microdata quirk (confirmed byte-for-byte identical), product URL shape (/s/<slug>/<numericId>, same as nordstrom.com, NOT /product/ as the pre-fix config assumed and which matched zero real links). Genuinely Rack-specific, not ported from Nordstrom: browse-page routing (/shop/<dept>/<category>/<slug>, not nordstrom.com's /browse/|/c/|/search), and card markup (a different frontend build entirely — <article> cards with CSS-module-hashed classes and zero data-element/data-testid attributes, where none of Nordstrom's own 'specific' selectors matched; findCards()/cardTitle()/cardBrand() were rebuilt from what's actually confirmed live on Rack's own pages, not ported wholesale). Does not use the BV main-world pagination fetch (explicitly excluded — see _isNordstromMainTab in background-v2.js; confirmed this exclusion holds against the real domain too, not just the wrong one). Reviews come from an interval + MutationObserver DOM poller reading the same reviewBody microdata Nordstrom uses, confirmed present on a real live product page (6 real review microdata nodes found). purchaseDetection: true reflects that the order-confirmation adapter's matches() now correctly recognizes nordstromrack.com (a one-line regex fix, same root cause) — the actual order-confirmation page/flow itself has NOT been live-validated, consistent with this project's standing rule against completing a real purchase during investigation.

Hard-capped at 90 raw reviews per product, always — fetchDeptStoreBVReviews (background-v2.js, shared with bloomingdales.com/urbanoutfitters.com/freepeople.com) loops a fixed 3 pages x 30 (`for (let page = 0; page < 3; page++)`, `limit = 30`) and only stops early if a page comes back empty or the running total already reaches the product's own TotalResults. Root cause of the 54-of-181 anomaly confirmed by re-running the exact fetch live against api.bazaarvoice.com (product 27228519, now 182 total reviews — one more than when first logged): the cap itself is hit cleanly every time (all 3 raw pages return a full 30 records, 90/90), so it was never an early stop, a partial page, or a rate limit. The gap is a filter *after* the fetch — the code keeps only records with non-empty ReviewText (`.filter(r => r.text)`), and a large share of Macy's BV reviews are ratings-only with no written text: only 23+16+14=53 of the 90 raw records had text this time (~29%, matching the original 54/181≈30%). Bloomingdale's/Urban Outfitters/Free People (see their notes) show zero equivalent textless-review attrition on the products tested — every one of their 90 raw records had text — so this looks like a Macy's catalog trait, not a shared BV-integration behavior, though only confirmed on this one product so far. No order-confirmation adapter exists for macys.com (not Shopify/WooCommerce/BigCommerce as far as verified) so purchase detection is not supported here.

Same fetchDeptStoreBVReviews code path as Macy's (background-v2.js) — hard-capped at 90 reviews per product (fixed 3 pages x 30, stops early only on an empty page or reaching the product's own TotalResults). Coverage on any given product = min(90, totalReviews) / totalReviews. Measured directly against the live BV Conversations API (api.bazaarvoice.com, reachable via plain curl — unlike Nordstrom, this fetch never touches bloomingdales.com itself so there's no bot-detection to work around): SPANX OnCore High-Waisted Shorts, product 1456334, 174 total reviews — all 3 pages returned a full 30 non-empty ReviewText each, so the code fetches exactly 90 of 174 (~52%), cleanly hitting the cap. No textless-review attrition like Macy's shows (see its notes) — every raw record here had text. 52% happens to clear "majority" on this one mid-volume product, but the same hard 90-review ceiling means coverage keeps shrinking as review count grows past it (see urbanoutfitters.com's 90/642 and 90/4,651 examples on the identical mechanism) — "limited" reflects that ceiling, not this one product. No order-confirmation adapter exists.

Reviews come from ASOS's own widget via DOM polling, not an API — coverage depends entirely on the widget rendering before the MutationObserver fires. A 2026-07-28 live scan found zero reviews on two tested ASOS DESIGN product pages, conflicting with earlier "working" reports; not yet reconciled (see RETAILER_SCRAPERS.md). Purchase confirmation detection (checkout/order-confirmation, order/success) is dedicated and reliable.

Direct Yotpo widget API fetch, uncapped up to 150 reviews. Measured live: 62 of 62 total reviews fetched (100%) on a tested product. Revolve's checkout is a custom PHP flow (orderconfirm.php), not yet built as an order-confirmation adapter.

Same Yotpo review platform as Revolve — shares fetchYotpoReviews()/_yotpoUpdateAndPublish() and the 150-review cap (5 pages x 30) in background-v2.js. Confirmed live via a real bestseller (Yumiko Romper Black, Shopify product ID 7079187939412): 1,762 total reviews on Yotpo, so this product's real coverage is 150/1,762 (~8.5%) — 'limited' reflects that ceiling on a genuinely high-review-volume product, not a default assumption (contrast Revolve's reviewData: true, whose tested product happened to have only 62 total reviews, under the cap). Yotpo's fit/sizing custom question is titled 'Fit' here vs. Revolve's 'Sizing' — both carry field_type: 'Size' (a Yotpo platform-level constant, confirmed identical across both accounts' live API responses), which is what _mapYotpoSizingValue's lookup was generalized to match on instead of title text. Product data (title/brand/description) reads from a data-yotpo-* bootstrap attribute set on the PDP (same pattern proven for Revolve) and from Product JSON-LD as a fallback; Princess Polly's own JSON-LD is @type: 'ProductGroup' rather than the bare 'Product' most other Shopify stores here embed, which required widening getProductJsonLd() (content.js) to accept that type as a fallback tier. Standard Shopify storefront (shopify-checkout-api-token meta tag + window.Shopify global both confirmed live), so purchase detection uses the same generic ORDER_CONFIRMATION_ADAPTERS 'shopify' adapter every approved Shopify-platform site gets — not independently re-verified against a completed real purchase on this specific retailer, per this project's standing rule against completing real transactions for verification. Browse-page grid is Algolia InstantSearch-rendered (li.ais-Hits-item tiles), not plain Shopify Liquid markup — findCards() (content.js) targets that class directly rather than the generic climb-from-product-link pattern, since this page also carries product links inside a mega-nav recommendations flyout and a hover-quick-add carousel that a naive climb would false-positive on. photoStyle: 'busy' and badgePosition: 'top-right' added 2026-08-12 per direct user request after live testing — badge legibility treatment matched to Free People's (both retailers shoot on-model lifestyle photography rather than white studio backgrounds), and the badge moved off the top-left corner specifically to avoid colliding with Princess Polly's own 'Selling Fast' promotional label, which renders top-left over the photo on some product cards.

Same fetchDeptStoreBVReviews code path as Macy's/Bloomingdale's (background-v2.js) — hard-capped at 90 reviews per product (fixed 3 pages x 30). Re-verified live via direct curl to api.bazaarvoice.com on both original test products: BDG Kayla Low-Rise Jeans (UO-89297493-000, now 642 total reviews, was 639) and a corset (UO-57537995-000, 4,651 total reviews, unchanged). Both hit the cap cleanly with all 90 raw records carrying non-empty ReviewText — no textless-review attrition like Macy's shows (see its notes). Coverage: 90/642 (~14%) and 90/4,651 (~2%). Storefront is a custom Vue app, not confirmed to run Shopify/WooCommerce/BigCommerce, so no order-confirmation adapter exists. badgePosition: 'bottom-left' set 2026-08-12 per direct user request (moved from the default top-left) — content.js's badgeAnchor for this retailer was updated at the same time to anchor to the tile's image wrapper rather than the whole card, mirroring Free People's existing fix for the identical issue on the same URBN tile component.

sites.limitationText: Fit badges can be harder to spot and show up less often here — Free People's product pages rely more on descriptive text than the structured data we usually read.
sites.notes: Sibling URBN brand sharing Urban Outfitters' exact fetchDeptStoreBVReviews code path (background-v2.js) — same hard 90-review-per-product cap (fixed 3 pages x 30). Measured live via direct curl to api.bazaarvoice.com: Good Karma High-Rise 7/8 Leggings (FP-52536018-000), 773 total reviews — hits the cap cleanly, all 90 raw records had non-empty ReviewText (matches Urban Outfitters' pattern, not Macy's textless-review issue — see their respective notes). Coverage: 90/773 (~11.6%). Most recently added integration in this codebase — re-verify this entry once it's had more live testing. photoStyle: "busy" — product photos are shot on location (gardens, stone buildings) rather than white studio backgrounds, which made the standard translucent browse badge illegible; gets the halo+shadow badge treatment instead (see content.css). No other retailer in this file is classified "busy" yet — deliberate, not an oversight (see content.js's photoStyle lookup comment). badgePosition: "bottom-left" — from the badge-positioning investigation (top-left was overlapping model faces on FP's portrait-style photography); FP was confirmed clean of any bottom-corner retailer UI (its own "Top Rated" badge and wishlist heart are both top corners). No other retailer is set to "bottom-left": Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack both have their own bottom-left promotional badges the moved badge would collide with, and the remaining retailers are unverified either way — deliberate, not an oversight. Known open gap: FP's own cropped/close-up shots (e.g. intimates) weren't re-verified live for bottom-left hand/ring overlap this session (bot-detection blocked repeat automated access) — accepted as a known limitation per the task's own call, since bottom-left is still expected to be a net improvement over the universal top-left face-overlap issue. fitScoring downgraded from true to "limited" (2026-08-06, task-directed, not independently re-measured this session): Free People product pages lean on descriptive text rather than structured data (titles/specs) Bustfit can reliably parse, which is also the root cause behind the busy-photoStyle and bottom-left-badgePosition workarounds above — the badge itself is harder to place and shows up less consistently as a result. limitationText carries the shopper-facing version of this; this note is the engineering-facing one. Should be re-verified with live measurement (e.g. badge-render success rate across a sample of FP product pages) rather than left on task-supplied rationale indefinitely.

Third URBN sibling brand, same fetchDeptStoreBVReviews code path as Urban Outfitters/Free People (background-v2.js) — same hard 90-review-per-product cap (fixed 3 pages x 30). Confirmed live via direct fetch to api.bazaarvoice.com on the Delphine Sweater Twofer Mini Dress (AN-4130916210343-000, 225 total reviews): hits the cap cleanly, all 30 raw records on the 3rd page (offset=60) had non-empty ReviewText — same clean pattern as UO/FP, not Macy's textless-review attrition. Coverage: 90/225 (40%). Storefront is the same custom Vue/Pinia PWA as UO/FP, not Shopify/WooCommerce/BigCommerce, so no order-confirmation adapter exists — this is a pre-existing, family-wide gap shared with UO/FP, not something specific to Anthropologie (see SESSION_HANDOFF.md's URBN order-confirmation follow-up). Browse grid (.c-pwa-tile-grid-tile / .c-pwa-tile-grid-inner), quickshop modal (.o-pwa-modal-overlay, data-qa-quickshop-button), and slow-mounting tile images are all confirmed live identical to UO/FP's component library. badgePosition: "bottom-left" — real collision found live, not assumed: 4 of 62 tiles on a real /dresses page carry a "Plus Sizes" label (.o-pwa-product-visual-badge__text) sitting almost exactly where a top-left badge would land (5px inset from the tile's own corner); bottom-left checked clean of any competing label. content.js's badgeAnchor was added at the same time, identical fallback chain to UO/FP's own, so "bottom" anchors to the photo, not the whole card.

First Gap Inc. brand added — oldnavy.com itself redirects to oldnavy.gap.com, a genuine subdomain of gap.com, not a separately-built site. Confirmed live (2026-08-27) that Gap.com shares the identical storefront platform: same data-testid component library (plp_product-card, plp_product-name, bv-reviews-root), same /browse/product.do?pid=... URL routing, same Product-details/Size-&-fit/Fabric-&-care heading structure, same <body> class naming convention (on/gap/br for Old Navy/Gap/Banana Republic) — tested side by side on both sites, not assumed. scrapeOldNavy() (content.js) reads title/brand from JSON-LD and description/fabric/fit signal from the three heading-anchored accordion panels, confirmed genuinely SSR via a raw fetch() of the page HTML (present without any JS/click). Browse grid: 194-229 cards under one shared parent (not URBN's unique-per-tile-wrapper shape), findCards()/cardTitle() work directly with no anchor-walking needed. sortStrategy: 'css-order' required — confirmed live via direct insertBefore repro (same test that caught Abercrombie's bug) that physically moving a card corrupts displaced cards' title text, even though this isn't a virtualized grid. No badgePosition/badgeAnchor override: confirmed live across a 194-card scan that neither top corner of the image has a competing label (no wishlist icon exists on these cards at all). Reviews: classic Bazaarvoice Conversations API, same fetchDeptStoreBVReviews() path as Macy's/Bloomingdale's/UO/Free People/Anthropologie (not Abercrombie's harder BFD-endpoint pattern) — confirmed live 2026-08-27 via the user's own real browser (the sandbox used for the rest of this investigation had an unrelated JS-execution gap that blocked observing this directly: zero .js requests loaded, a real Add to Bag click had no effect — resolved once tested outside the sandbox, both reviews and Add to Bag work normally). Deployment name 'old-navy' confirmed directly (its bvapi.js returns real content, pointed to by the review JSON's own SourceClient:'old-navy' field); the passkey embedded there was independently confirmed live to also return real data, used as fallbackPasskey. reviewSampleCap (90 = pageSize 30 x maxPages 3) matches the same shape as every other dept-store BV retailer — confirmed live via the actual extracted fetchDeptStoreBVReviews() run against the real API (not a reimplementation) that all 3 pages return real data; real yield on the one product tested was 67 of 90 slots (some raw records were textless and filtered, same pattern as Macy's, not the cleaner UO/FP/Anthropologie case). No SecondaryRatings fit-slider data was found on any review tested (_extractBVFitRating returned null for all 67) — not yet clear whether Old Navy's BV deployment carries this custom dimension at all; worth re-checking on a different product before concluding it never does. purchaseDetection is false: the add-to-bag/checkout transition type (full nav vs. SPA) was confirmed observable now that testing moved outside the sandbox, but the checkout-to-confirmation step itself was deliberately not tested, per the standing rule against completing real purchases — still an open item, not guessed at.

Second Gap Inc. brand, ported from oldnavy.gap.com's confirmed build (2026-09-01) — same data-testid component library, /browse/product.do?pid=... routing, Product-details/Size-&-fit/Fabric-&-care heading structure, <body class="gap">, all independently re-confirmed live (not assumed from the earlier spot-check): 200/200 and 195/195 cards resolved across two categories, SSR confirmed via raw fetch() with no JS. One real divergence from the original investigation: a fresh, more aggressive insertBefore repro (28-39 cards moved at once, mimicking _applyPicksSort, vs. the original single-card-move test) produced zero corruption this time, unlike the corruption the original spot-check found in August — both results are documented honestly in RETAILER_SCRAPERS.md rather than picking one; sortStrategy: 'css-order' is kept regardless since it's strictly safe either way. Reviews: classic Bazaarvoice Conversations API, confirmed live — but the deployment name is NOT derivable from the brand name the way Old Navy's and Banana Republic's are ('old-navy', 'banana-republic'): 'gap', 'GAP', 'gap.com', and 'gapinc' all 404'd against display.ugc.bazaarvoice.com. The real name, 'the-gap', was only found by triggering the actual on-page widget script tag in a real browser. Passkey extracted from that deployment's bvapi.js, independently confirmed live: Filter=ProductId:911400 returned TotalResults:122 with real fit-relevant review text. No SecondaryRatings fit-slider data found on the product tested, same as Old Navy. Checkout transition confirmed live (new information Old Navy's own investigation never resolved): clicking Checkout after Add to Bag navigates www.gap.com -> secure-www.gap.com, a full page cross-subdomain navigation, not a client-side SPA transition — stopped there per the standing rule against completing a real purchase. purchaseDetection stays false: no order-confirmation adapter built, consistent with the rest of the Gap Inc. family.

Third Gap Inc. brand, ported from oldnavy.gap.com's confirmed build (2026-09-01) — same data-testid component library, heading structure, <body class="br">, JSON-LD brand.name "Banana Republic", all confirmed live on Banana Republic's own pages independently (not assumed from Gap's confirmation). One real, brand-specific divergence found: on categories with more than ~165 total products, a contiguous tail of plp_product-card elements renders as a completely empty shell (zero children, no plp_product-name ever appears) that doesn't resolve even after aggressive scroll/scrollIntoView/multi-second waits — confirmed reproducible across two categories and two independent browser environments, with the exact stall point varying between runs (165, then 27 on a re-test), meaning it's a throttled/rate-limited progressive loader stalling at a variable point, not a fixed hard cap. Confirmed NOT a sandbox-wide artifact: Gap.com hit 200/200 clean in the identical environments in the same session. No special-case code was added for this — content.js's existing _injectBadgeOnCard() already treats an empty-title card as 'still hydrating' (leaves bfScore unset, not 'none'), so browseScrollObserver's mutation watch retries it automatically on every later DOM mutation, the same generic mechanism already covering Urban Outfitters' slow tile-mounting and Revolve's structural badgeAnchor case. Live-validated specifically against a >165-product category with patient real-time waiting (not just the first few seconds): previously-empty cards do eventually populate and get scored once the mechanism is given real time — see RETAILER_SCRAPERS.md for the measured before/after counts, not just a theoretical claim that the mechanism exists. Reviews: classic Bazaarvoice Conversations API, deployment name 'banana-republic' confirmed live (this one did match the hyphenated-brand-name convention, unlike Gap's). Passkey extracted from bvapi.js, independently confirmed live: Filter=ProductId:899792 returned TotalResults:2 with real review text AND a SecondaryRatings block including a literal 'bra' fit dimension — not seen on any other Gap Inc. brand's reviews checked so far. That 'bra' dimension is not currently surfaced anywhere: background-v2.js's _extractBVFitRating() only matches SecondaryRatings keys/Ids containing 'fit', so it's silently dropped the same way any other non-fit-labeled dimension is on any retailer using this shared function — confirmed by reading the code, not built into anything special here per this round's scope. Checkout transition confirmed live, same pattern as Gap: bananarepublic.gap.com -> secure-bananarepublic.gap.com, full page cross-subdomain navigation — stopped there, no purchase completed. purchaseDetection stays false, consistent with the rest of the Gap Inc. family.

Not a port of any existing retailer — a genuinely different platform/DOM shape, built specifically to test the review-weighted-scoring hypothesis for bras/sports-bras/fitted tops (see bustfit-swim-activewear-category-notes.md). Confirmed live (2026-09-01): <body class="">, <html class="lll-base">, both clean of Abercrombie-style page-state collision, including with a filter panel open. JSON-LD is ProductGroup, handled by getProductJsonLd()'s existing fallback tier with no code changes. Fabric/construction/support text lives in one accordion container, [class*="product-education-accordions"] — confirmed live across 3 real bras this single selector's textContent captures fabric percentages, support-level text ("Intended for medium-impact activities"), and real construction bullets ("Laser-cut pocket openings for optional, removable cups") in one read; client-hydrated (0/6 details panels present immediately after navigation, need a real wait), not in a pre-JS raw fetch, but no MAIN-world scripting needed — same post-hydration DOM read every other retailer already uses. Browse grid: every tile has its own unique parent (distinctParents === totalTiles, same shape as Urban Outfitters/Revolve, not Gap Inc.'s shared-parent shape) — sortAnchor (`el => el.parentElement`) confirmed live to resolve all 40 tiles to one shared grid container. A 7-card insertBefore reorder test came back clean (0 corruption), but sortStrategy: 'css-order' is kept as the safe default regardless. Reviews: classic Bazaarvoice Conversations API, but everything about locating it was harder than any retailer built so far — bvapi.js needs a capitalized deployment name ("Lululemon", confirmed live the lowercase form 404s), found only by reading the real on-page loader's own referenced-URL list (a newer BV SDK version, "bv-loader", not the older webpack bvapi.js bundle every other retailer here uses). The passkey itself is stored under a numeric-suffixed unquoted key (`passkey7:"..."`) that no existing _BV_PASSKEY_PATTERNS entry matched — a new pattern was added. ProductId is a human-readable slug (`bazaarVoiceID`, e.g. "Wunder_Train_Mesh_Back_Bra_Medium_BC"), not numeric and not derivable from the URL, found only inside the page's Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ state blob — no DOM attribute carries it anywhere on the page (checked). Live-validated end to end on 2 bras beyond the ones checked during investigation (lululemon Focuser Halter Bra: 3 real reviews confirmed via the actual Conversations API call; Wundermost Ultra-Soft Nulu Triangle Bralette: 0 reviews, confirmed genuinely zero via the product's own missing JSON-LD aggregateRating field, not a broken extraction). Review-relevance investigation (see RETAILER_SCRAPERS.md and bustfit-swim-activewear-category-notes.md for full detail): bust-relevant review-text rate measured at 33-40% across 2 bras (196 and 496 total reviews) and 1 fitted tank (7,737 total reviews), versus 17% on a legging product used as a negative control — and every one of the legging "hits" was confirmed to be a false positive (generic leg/waist "compression"/"support" language, zero actual bust content), while the bra/tank hits included real cup-size self-identification and fit-mechanism detail. Reviews also carry a real structured fit dimension (SecondaryRatings.Fit_22, a 5-point slider) that background-v2.js's existing _extractBVFitRating() already picks up correctly via its /fit/i key match, no code changes needed. Checkout transition confirmed live via performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0].type (not inferred): shop.lululemon.com/shop/mybag -> shop.lululemon.com/shop/checkout, a full page navigation but same-origin, no cross-subdomain jump like Gap Inc.'s secure-* pattern — stopped at the checkout page itself before any address/payment entry. purchaseDetection stays false: no order-confirmation adapter built, no saved reference page exists.

No third-party review platform exists to call directly — DOM-scraped only. Logged-out users get a one-shot synchronous scrape of the ~13 reviews present on the PDP; logged-in users get an additional hidden-iframe pagination fetch of up to 5 pages (~50 reviews total). reviewSampleCap (50) reflects the logged-in ceiling (AMAZON_REVIEW_PAGE_COUNT x 10 in content.js) — the only one of the two figures backed by an actual code constant, so it's what validate-supported-sites.js checks; the logged-out ~13 is an empirical DOM-count observation, not a fixed cap in code. Purchase detection (2026-08-04) is NOT one of the ORDER_CONFIRMATION_ADAPTERS in content.js — live investigation found automated add-to-cart/checkout actions silently no-op'd by Amazon's bot mitigation, so there's no reachable confirmation page to build selectors against. Instead it diffs the real 'Your Orders' page (selectors verified live against a real logged-in account) against a locally-seeded baseline of order numbers, routing genuinely-new orders through the same processOrderConfirmation() pipeline every other retailer uses (background-v2.js). Known limitations: grocery/pickup orders (Whole Foods-style 'PICKUP AT' cards) render products as image-only alt text with no title-link text and are skipped entirely, since they're not clothing anyway; a purchase placed in the exact window before the very first seed snapshot completes is an inherent blind spot of snapshot-based seeding, not a bug; only a single shipment/status per order card was confirmed live, so multi-shipment orders with per-item delivery dates are unverified. See RETAILER_SCRAPERS.md → Amazon for the full design writeup.

Product scraper (scrapeAbercrombie(), content.js) reads standard Product JSON-LD (name/description/image/aggregateRating, no brand field — single-brand store, hardcoded) plus a server-rendered 'Details & Material' accordion panel ([data-testid="fabric-care-mfe"] h4) for fabric composition (e.g. 'BODY: 85% POLYESTER, 15% ELASTANE') — confirmed live via a raw fetch() of the page HTML that this is fully SSR despite the accordion UI, no click/wait needed. Browse-grid is unusually clean structurally: [data-testid="catalog-product-card"] cards wrap both the image and [data-testid="catalog-product-card-name"] title directly, no badgeAnchor/sortAnchor override needed. Order-confirmation adapter (ORDER_CONFIRMATION_ADAPTERS 'abercrombie', content.js) matches the custom-platform /shop/OrderConfirmationDisplayView URL (not Shopify/WooCommerce/BigCommerce). Verified end-to-end (not just piece-by-piece) against a real saved 4-item order: matches()+scrape() run together produce the correct ORDER_CONFIRMATION_DETECTED message, and that exact message was fed into the real processOrderConfirmation() (background-v2.js, via a Node harness with mocked chrome.storage/chrome.alarms) — confirmed correct matching/dedup-by-productId, order-history persistence, feedback-alarm scheduling, and duplicate-order rejection. The item list renders TWICE on this page (a desktop right-rail summary and a small-screen summary, both always mounted, CSS-toggled for responsive layout) — an unscoped query returns 8 elements for 4 real items, so the adapter scopes to #right-rail-shopping-bag and dedupes by data-sku, not name — this order has two genuinely different SKUs (different colors) sharing one product name, which a name-based dedup would have wrongly collapsed into one (and did, in a deliberate contrast test). Estimated-delivery text never carries a year (e.g. 'Wed, 08/19') — _parseAbercrombieDeliveryDate() infers it, rolling FORWARD a year when the guess lands more than a day in the past (the mirror image of Amazon's order-history date logic, which rolls BACK — verified via a Node repro that blindly reusing Amazon's rollback direction here would silently misdate an order placed right at the December/January boundary). A real completed pickup order was never detected in production (root cause never conclusively pinned down — adapter and matcher logic both re-verified correct against the real saved page, but no page-console evidence survived from the actual failure moment); a retry (mirroring the product-page scrape retry pattern) and Sentry drift instrumentation on the detection path (isOrderConfirmationPage/matchOrderConfirmationAdapter/handleOrderConfirmation/SPA-navigation-never-rerun) were added as risk mitigation and future-signal, not a confirmed fix — treat purchase detection as resolved-pending-real-signal until a Sentry event or a clean real-purchase confirmation closes it out. Reviews: the on-page widget is Bazaarvoice, via a newer 'BFD' endpoint (apps.bazaarvoice.com/bfd/v1/clients/abercrombie/...) rather than the passkey-based Conversations API every other BV retailer here uses. The numeric product id comes directly from the SSR HTML (data-bv-product-id). The endpoint requires a 'bv-bfd-token' request header (value 'displaycode,main_site,en_US' — a static value derived from the same displaycode already used in the URL, not a session-bound secret) that a plain fetch() doesn't send by default; omitting it produces a real, live 401 regardless of network/environment. This was the actual root cause of every earlier 'reviews not loading' investigation this project did — confirmed live 2026-08-26 by capturing the real on-page widget's successful request in DevTools and diffing it header-by-header against fetchAbercrombieBVReviews()'s request; every prior theory (sandbox-specific IP block, widget-only page-2-click trigger dependency, pageSize hard-capped at 8) was a plausible-sounding but incorrect explanation for the same underlying symptom. fetchAbercrombieBVReviews() (background-v2.js) sends this header and uses Nordstrom-style MAIN-world scripting (needed because the endpoint's CORS response only allows abercrombie.com's own origin to read it, not a background-worker fetch). With the header present, fetchAbercrombieBVReviews() has no dependency on the widget's own page-2-click-to-load pattern — its request loop is unconditional and already starts at offset=0. reviewSampleCap (90) reflects up to 3 requests of limit=30 each (args: [numericId, 30, 3]), stopping early once TotalResults is reached — the same pageSize/page-count shape fetchDeptStoreBVReviews() already uses for Nordstrom/Macy's/Bloomingdale's/Urban Outfitters/Free People, chosen deliberately over guessing at a higher untested per-request limit. The earlier 'pageSize hard-capped at 8' finding was a misread: those tests predated the header fix, so every call 401'd regardless of limit and the failure got misattributed to page size. The circuit breaker (chrome.storage.local, survives service-worker restarts, 6-hour cooldown on first failure) is kept in place as cheap insurance against a genuine future edge case (e.g. a real per-IP rate limit under real load, or Bazaarvoice changing this token's format again) — verified via a Node harness that it makes zero network attempts during an active cooldown, never self-extends, resumes correctly after the window expires, and does not trip on a legitimate zero-review product. Full pipeline — fetch through MAIN-world scripting across all 3 pages, circuit breaker, dedup, scoring, bust-relevant filtering, review-summary generation, and rendering in both the panel's Community tab and Fit Analysis tab — confirmed live end-to-end through the actual packaged extension on two real product pages (2026-08-26): a 30-review product (single page) and a 90-review product (all 3 pages, confirming offset=30/60 both return real data, not just offset=0).
